Taken together, our data suggest that the high conservation of fis gene duplication results from the need for fine-tuned control of Legionella virulence in response to its different environmental and human hosts, rather than from functional redundancy to circumvent deleterious fis mutations.

title: Trans-Acting Factors in circRNA Biogenesis-Potential Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets for Receptive and Cancerous Endometrium.
abstract: Dysregulated circRNA expression is considered one of the main molecular regulatory mechanisms for the processes in an organism, among which are endometrial cancerogenesis and the establishment of endometrial receptivity. The cancerous and receptive endometrium have been described as opposites-the first characterized by intense proliferation and the lowest differentiation, while the latter is regarded as the most highly differentiated. CircRNAs are non-coding RNA molecules, represented by a closed loop with no 5' cap and 3' poly(A) tail structure, which makes them undistinguishable from most endonucleases and ensures them a longer half-life than their linear cognates, influencing the expression of miRNA and genes. CircRNA biogenesis is regulated by cis-molecules and trans-acting factors (TAFs). Our attention was on TAFs-key molecular switches in circRNA biogenesis, less noted in the literature and involved in studies concerning the endometrium, which can change the bias between circular and linear counterparts, affecting the cellular structure and function. Today, over 2600 TAFs are involved in the ubiquitous disorders of transcriptional programs. TAFs participate in cellular proliferation, differentiation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and angiogenesis. They play a pivotal role in developmental and oncogenic pathways and influence both cancer development and progression, and the establishment of endometrial receptivity. An in-depth and detailed analysis of the TAFs could facilitate both diagnostics and treatment of EC (endometrial cancer) and ER (endometrial receptivity) for RIF (repeated implantation failure) cases' solution. Future research is necessary to broaden the knowledge about the application capacity of TAFs as circRNA modulators in EC and ER, and to study their potential as biomarkers and therapeutic molecules.

title: Genomic Context and Stage-Associated Expression of Long Non-Coding RNAs During Bovine Conceptus Elongation.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate gene expression and developmental processes, yet their expression and potential functions during bovine conceptus elongation are poorly understood. This study characterized stage-associated lncRNA expression, genomic context, associations with neighboring protein-coding genes, and sex-associated expression during this developmental window. Methods: RNA-sequencing data were generated from bovine conceptuses collected at ovoid (n = 6), tubular (n = 7), and filamentous (n = 7) developmental stages and analyzed to identify differentially expressed lncRNAs. Stage-associated lncRNAs were classified by genomic relationships with nearby protein-coding genes, and correlations with neighboring genes were assessed to identify candidate local regulatory relationships. Coding potential and spliced-read evidence were assessed for each lncRNA. In individually sequenced tubular and filamentous conceptuses, sex was assigned using XIST and Y-linked gene expression, followed by assessment of sex-associated transcription. Results: Forty-two lncRNAs were differentially expressed during conceptus elongation. Most changes occurred between the ovoid and tubular stages and were maintained through the filamentous stage. Genomic-context classification and expression-correlation analyses identified four candidate local relationships between lncRNAs and neighboring protein-coding genes, one of which (MKLN1) was robust to adjustment for donor, consistent with potential cis-regulatory activity. Coding-potential analysis supported the non-coding status of these transcripts, although one sex-associated locus showed a clear protein-coding signature and is likely misannotated. Sex-associated analyses identified female-biased XIST expression and widespread female-biased X-linked transcription. Conclusions: This study provides the first characterization of lncRNA expression during bovine conceptus elongation. The identified stage-associated lncRNAs and candidate local regulatory relationships provide targets for functional investigation of mechanisms supporting conceptus development. Sex-associated transcriptional patterns further support incomplete X-chromosome dosage compensation during this developmental interval.

title: lncRNA MANCR Isoforms Selectively Contribute to Epigenomic and p53-Responsive Transcriptional Control in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
abstract: Background: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are important regulators of gene expression and are frequently dysregulated in cancer. The mitotically associated lncRNA MANCR is highly expressed in aggressive cancers and contributes to genomic instability in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but the molecular mechanisms underlying its activity remain poorly defined. Methods: Here we integrated computational and experimental approaches to examine the structure and regulatory interactions of MANCR isoforms. RNA-sequencing was performed in MDA-MB-231 and MCF10A cells and integrated with publicly available breast cancer transcriptomic datasets. MANCR-associated chromatin was characterized by ChIRP-seq in MDA-MB-231 cells. Computational analyses of patient data, sequence motifs, and molecular modeling suggested an interaction between MANCR and p53, which was investigated using RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (RIP-seq) and a p53-responsive luciferase reporter assay. Results: Analysis of transcriptomic datasets revealed tumor-type-specific expression patterns for seven MANCR isoforms in breast cancer cell lines. Computational prediction of RNA secondary structures identified conserved structural features across isoforms, suggesting potential functional specialization. We identify p53 as a MANCR-associated protein through computational docking and RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (RIP-seq) and demonstrate that MANCR depletion reduces p53-dependent transcriptional activity. Chromatin isolation by RNA purification sequencing (ChIRP-seq) revealed 1250 genomic regions associated with MANCR, including enrichment of p53 consensus motifs and GC-rich sequence elements. Motif analysis further identified candidate sequence features associated with MANCR-occupied chromatin regions. Conclusions: Together, these results suggest that MANCR may contribute to transcriptional regulation in TNBC in an isoform-specific manner through interactions with chromatin and p53 signaling pathways.

title: Circular RNAs in metabolic reprogramming and therapy resistance in prostate cancer: emerging links to the tumor immune microenvironment.
abstract: Therapy resistance in prostate cancer can emerge at different disease stages; castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is one clinically important state, and resistance to individual therapies may overlap but is not synonymous with CRPC. Metabolic reprogramming-including changes in glycolysis, de novo lipogenesis, glutamine metabolism, and mitochondrial homeostasis-has been implicated in prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance, although the strength of evidence varies across pathways and treatment settings. CircRNAs have been reported to modulate selected metabolic nodes in prostate cancer, although direct links between circRNA-associated metabolic changes and acquired therapy resistance are established only in a subset of studies. This review evaluates circRNAs as candidate regulators of selected metabolic processes in therapy-resistant prostate cancer. Mechanistically, individual circRNAs have been associated with selected metabolic changes through proposed miRNA-mediated interactions and, in some reports, peptide translation or protein scaffolding. These metabolic changes could, in principle, intersect with immunometabolic programmes such as lactate-associated suppression, lipid-linked macrophage states, and adenosine signalling; however, direct evidence that individual circRNAs control these immune-cell processes in CRPC remains limited, as detailed in the evidence tiers later in this review. Therapy-specific resistance networks are organised for enzalutamide/androgen deprivation therapy, docetaxel, PARP inhibitors and radiotherapy, distinguishing metabolism-dependent axes from signalling, mitotic, DNA-repair and exosome-propagated routes. Beyond mechanistic insights, circRNAs hold promise as non-invasive liquid-biopsy biomarkers and as druggable targets amenable to antisense oligonucleotide silencing, mimic delivery, and engineered circRNA vaccines. Major barriers to clinical translation include incomplete multi-therapy metabolic maps, sparse stage-resolved evidence across the hormone-sensitive→CRPC→neuroendocrine continuum, and unresolved delivery, safety, and regulatory challenges. Overall, current evidence supports circRNA-associated metabolic vulnerabilities as a promising preclinical research framework; however, circRNA-targeted metabolic interventions for therapy-resistant prostate cancer have not yet been clinically validated.

title: Dissecting the role of FLNA cleavage and signaling in mediating calpeptin effects in neuroendocrine tumors.
abstract: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare malignancies with a rising incidence and heterogeneous clinical behavior, posing significant challenges to diagnosis and treatment. The urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies is increasingly evident. Filamin A (FLNA), a cytoskeletal protein involved in cancer progression and inflammatory signaling, is cleaved by calpain to generate a 90 kDa C-terminal fragment (FLNACT), whose functional role in NETs remains unclear. The calpain inhibitor calpeptin prevents FLNA cleavage. This study investigates the role of FLNA cleavage and the effects of calpeptin in NET progression using western blotting, RNA sequencing, functional assays, and patient-derived NET organoid models. We found that NET cells express both full-length FLNA and FLNACT, with both localized in the cytoplasm. Calpeptin reduces FLNACT expression and inhibits proliferation and viability in NET models. Its inhibitory effect on cell migration was observed specifically in H727 cells. RNA sequencing identified numerous calpeptin-regulated genes. Comparing the top 500 most significantly altered genes in QGP-1 and H727 cells, we identified 115 genes consistently downregulated and 148 upregulated. Among them, CEACAM5, CDC6, and EGR1 were affected by FLNA silencing in QGP1, while CCNE1, CDC6, ATF3, and EGR1 were influenced in H727. KEGG pathway analysis highlighted cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions in QGP-1 cells, cell cycle regulation in H727 cells, and TGF-β signaling in both models. Calpeptin downregulated TGFBR2 and TGFB3 in both cell lines, with FLNA mediating this effect only in H727 cells. Additionally, it reduced IL5RA in QGP1 and IL17RB in H727, with FLNA involvement limited to H727 cells. Expression of a calpain-resistant FLNA mutant indicated that most transcriptional effects of calpeptin were not fully recapitulated by inhibition of FLNA cleavage alone. In patient-derived NET organoids, calpeptin reduced viability and arrested organoid growth, without inducing a significant increase in caspase-3/7 activity, supporting a predominantly cytostatic rather than pro-apoptotic effect. These findings highlight the complex interplay between calpain activity, FLNA function, and FLNA proteolysis in NETs and support further preclinical investigation of calpain inhibition as a potential therapeutic approach.

title: Homozygous SPOUT1 variants cause protein destabilization, resulting in epileptic encephalopathy.
abstract: SPOUT1, a member of the SPOUT methyltransferase superfamily, plays a critical role in RNA methylation and cell cycle regulation. We investigated the impact of bi-allelic missense variants in SPOUT1 in three unrelated families with infants presenting with intractable seizures, microcephaly, and severe global developmental delay. Homozygosity mapping and whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing identified three homozygous variants: c.292G > A (p.Gly98Ser), c.836T > C (p.Phe279Ser), and c.1058 C > T (p.Thr353Met). Segregation analysis confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance. In-silico structural modeling predicted that all three variants destabilize SPOUT1, likely impairing protein folding, cofactor binding, and promoting degradation. Functional studies in patient-derived fibroblasts demonstrated markedly reduced SPOUT1 protein levels in the nucleus and cytoplasm along with decreased nuclear aggregates of SPOUT1. These genetic, structural, and cellular data establish a shared destabilization of SPOUT1 protein across independent variants. The resulting SPOUT1 deficiency, termed SpADMiSS (SPOUT1-Associated Developmental Delay, Microcephaly, Seizures, and Short Stature) defines a distinct neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, microcephaly, and severe global developmental delay. These findings support the essential role of SPOUT1 in neuronal development and demonstrate how destabilizing missense variants impair SPOUT1 nuclear localization, providing novel insights for the observed clinical phenotype. Understanding SPOUT1 dysfunction offers opportunities for further mechanistic studies and may inform the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for severe childhood epilepsies.

title: Near telomere to telomere genome assembly of Fujian Longyan Shan-ma duck (Anas platyrhynchos).
abstract: The domestic duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is an economically important poultry species and a valuable model for studying avian domestication and trait diversification. High-quality reference genomes have been generated for meat-type ducks, including Pekin duck. By contrast, genomic resources for laying-type breeds remain limited, constraining comparative analyses across divergent production types. Here, we present a near telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly of the female Fujian Longyan Shan-ma duck (A. platyrhynchos-FJLY), a representative laying-type breed. Using PacBio HiFi (~107×), Oxford Nanopore ultra-long (~35×), and Hi-C (~80×) sequencing, we assembled a 1.28 Gb genome anchored to 41 chromosomes, including 39 autosomes and the Z and W chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 79.80 Mb and an anchoring rate of 98.55%. We predicted 18,749 protein-coding genes, of which 99.63% received functional annotations. The assembly showed high completeness, with 99.36% complete BUSCOs using the aves_odb12 dataset, and high base-level accuracy, with QV values greater than 39. Using this reference, we also re-analysed public ovarian RNA-seq data and generated a gene-level read count matrix and a catalogue of differentially expressed genes between high- and low-egg-number duck groups, which are provided as supplementary datasets. This genome assembly and its associated annotation and transcriptomic datasets expand genomic resources for laying-type ducks and provide a foundation for future comparative genomic and trait-related studies.

title: CDK12/13 inhibition by CTX-439 creates a targetable BCL-2/BCL-xL dependency.
abstract: CDK12/13 regulate transcription through phosphorylation of Serine 2 (S2) in the C-terminal domain of RNA polymerase II and have emerged as potential therapeutic targets in cancer. Here, we report the development of CTX-439, an orally bioavailable, ATP-competitive small-molecule inhibitor of CDK12/13. CTX-439 inhibits S2 phosphorylation and downregulates genes involved in DNA damage repair, resulting in antitumor activity in vitro and in vivo, including in breast cancer patient-derived xenograft models. A CRISPR activation screen identified the anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family members BCL-2 and BCL-xL as mediators of resistance to CTX-439. Accordingly, combined inhibition of CDK12/13 and BCL-2/BCL-xL induced apoptosis and enhanced tumor growth suppression in xenograft models. Mechanistically, CTX-439 reduces MCL1 protein levels through transcriptional readthrough, shifting cell survival dependency toward BCL-2 and BCL-xL. Together, these findings identify a vulnerability induced by CDK12/13 inhibition and provide a rationale for combining CTX-439 with BCL-2/BCL-xL inhibitors.

title: Region-dependent matricellular remodeling in failed cardiac xenografts from α1,3-galactosyltransferase knockout pig.
abstract: Recent clinical milestones in cardiac xenotransplantation have highlighted that non-immunological graft failure, characterized by "xenograft cardiomegaly" and rapid structural collapse, remains a critical barrier. This study investigated the spatial expression patterns of matricellular proteins (MCPs) during terminal cardiac xenograft remodeling. Heterotopic cardiac xenotransplantation was performed using a α1,3-galactosyltransferase knockout (GTKO) pig donor and a cynomolgus monkey recipient. Following graft failure at posttransplantation day 9, myocardial tissues were collected from three anatomical regions (basal, midventricular, and apical). We performed transcriptomic profiling via RNA sequencing and validated the region-specific expression of MCPs (thrombospondin 1 [TSP-1], secreted protein acidic and rich in cysteine [SPARC], tenascin-C, and periostin-2C) using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemistry. Despite the absence of hyperacute rejection, the failed graft exhibited extensive myocardial infarction and interstitial fibrosis. Transcriptomic analysis revealed a global upregulation of MCPs in the xenograft. Notably, regional validation demonstrated a spatial intensification of these molecular signals, with significantly higher expression levels of TSP-1, tenascin-C, SPARC, and periostin-2C in the apical myocardium compared to the basal region. These findings suggest that regional MCP induction may reflect localized remodeling responses associated with mechanical stress and/or regional injury within the failing graft. Our findings demonstrate region-dependent upregulation of MCPs in failed cardiac xenografts, particularly within the apical myocardium. These observations suggest that MCP-associated remodeling may contribute to early structural deterioration in cardiac xenografts. Further studies are required to determine whether modulation of MCP-associated remodeling may improve long-term graft stability.

title: N6-Methyladenosine Modification of TMEM259 mRNA: A Critical Regulator of Endoplasmic Reticulum Homeostasis in Glioma.
abstract: Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) homeostasis ensures proper protein folding, while ER stress activates the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) and ER-associated degradation (ERAD) to restore proteostasis and support cell survival. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) of the METTL3-silenced glioma transcriptome revealed a pronounced depletion of ER homeostasis-associated gene sets. Aptly, silencing METTL3 exacerbated ER stress, as reflected by elevated expression of IRE1, GRP78, ATF4, CHOP, and ATF6, and increased ATF6-Luc reporter activity, whereas overexpression of METTL3 suppressed these stress responses. METTL3 silencing further compromised ERAD, reflected by the increased accumulation and reduced ubiquitination of NHK (null Hong Kong variant of α-1 antitrypsin), a well-established ERAD substrate. An integrated analysis identified TMEM259/Membralin as the primary METTL3 target. Anti-METTL3 or anti-m6A immunoprecipitation brought down TMEM259 mRNA in a METTL3-dependent manner, with m6A modification promoting transcript stability. METTL3 binding and m6A modification required two m6A sites in the 11th exon of TMEM259. Further, recruitment of HuR, an m6A reader protein, is required for m6A-dependent stabilization. Additionally, exogenous overexpression of TMEM259 rescued the phenotypes of METTL3-silenced cells. Thus, we establish that the METTL3/TMEM259 axis promotes ERAD, thereby maintaining ER homeostasis in glioma.

title: mirCCC: Repression-aware graph learning for miRNA-mediated cell-cell communication inference.
abstract: Cell-cell communication analyses usually focus on protein ligands and receptors and therefore miss extracellular vesicle transfer of microRNAs, an important route of signalling in cancer. Here we show that microRNA-mediated communication can be inferred from standard single-cell RNA sequencing by detecting coordinated decreases in the expression of validated miRNA target genes. We developed mirCCC, a computational framework that estimates cell-specific microRNA activity, models cellular sending and receiving capacity for extracellular vesicle transfer, and learns microRNA-resolved communication graphs from transcriptomic data. In synthetic benchmarks with strong confounding signals, mirCCC improved whereas all comparison methods declined. Applied to a human colorectal cancer atlas, mirCCC recovered known colorectal cancer-associated microRNAs and identified stromal- and myeloid-to-epithelial communication converging on a plasticity program linked to TGF-β and Wnt/β-catenin signalling. These results provide a practical route for studying extracellular vesicle-mediated communication in existing single-cell atlases.

title: mRNA Vaccines for Colorectal Cancer: Antigen Design, Nanodelivery, and Clinical Translation.
abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines offer a flexible approach to colorectal cancer (CRC) immunotherapy, with applications ranging from postoperative residual disease to metastatic cancer. This narrative review examines antigen selection, RNA engineering, nanodelivery, and clinical development, drawing on literature available through 21 October 2026. Tumor-associated antigens, shared driver mutations, and personalized neoantigens offer different advantages in population coverage, specificity, and manufacturing. Their activity also depends on RNA chemistry and carrier design, including lipid composition, endosomal release, APC targeting, tissue distribution, stability, and repeated dosing. Early clinical studies have demonstrated antigen-specific T-cell responses in selected patients, while randomized melanoma data provide a benchmark for combining vaccination with checkpoint blockade. The termination of the CRC adjuvant autogene cevumeran monotherapy trial highlights the difficulty of translating immune priming into recurrence prevention. Antigen heterogeneity, impaired HLA presentation, stromal exclusion, and liver-associated immune suppression remain important barriers in CRC. Advances in neoantigen prediction, self-amplifying RNA, and mechanism-based combinations may improve vaccine design, but their clinical value will depend on disease-specific trials that account for manufacturing feasibility and established oncological endpoints. The available evidence remains heterogeneous, with small CRC cohorts and limited randomized outcomes; the non-systematic search also introduces potential selection bias.

title: Trem2R47H and reduced TREM2 expression both mimic human Alzheimer's disease signatures in mice.
abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) loss of function variants are associated with late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD). We molecularly assessed mice with the missense variant, R47H (Trem2*R47HHSS), and mice with additional cryptic splicing and reduced Trem2 expression (Trem2*R47H) while comparing relevance to human LOAD. The aberrant splice acceptor site in the Trem2*R47H mouse was humanized resulting in the Trem2*R47H humanized splice site (Trem2*R47HHSS) mouse. RNA sequencing was performed on mouse brain tissue and signatures were compared to human post mortem brain expression in LOAD cohorts. Trem2*R47H mice had alternative splicing leading to reduced Trem2 expression; Trem2*R47HHSS mice expressed Trem2 at wild-type transcript and protein levels. Both models correlated with similar LOAD-associated signatures, and had similar effects on immune response, synapse, and vasculature biodomains. The Trem2*R47H model additionally affected extracellular matrix and myelination signatures. We demonstrated that Trem2*R47H and Trem2*R47HHSS mice are complementary models for the study of molecular contributions to LOAD pathology.

title: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery.
abstract: Accurate cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing is sensitive to upstream parameters often selected heuristically. We introduce scBOA, a two-stage framework that uses Bayesian optimization to select workflow parameters against a prespecified objective and reruns the selected configuration for reference-assisted analysis. Its configurable objectives combine annotation purity, marker concordance and transcriptomic cohesion, enabling fine-grained or conservative solutions. Optional extensions support low-confidence-cell refinement and multi-sample integration. Across simulations and fluorescence-activated cell sorting datasets of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, pancreas and adult heart, we compare Gaussian-process scBOA with 14 alternative parameter-selection and clustering strategies. We show that performance depends on the objective, workflow, reference hierarchy and vocabulary, consensus-label construction and partition granularity. We find that scBOA is not uniformly superior, but shows strong aggregate performance when annotation targets align with biological structure. We apply a mouse Huntington's disease dataset as an exploratory stress test of integration and reference mapping. Overall, we demonstrate that scBOA provides reproducible, objective-driven workflow optimization for reference-assisted single-cell analysis.

title: An Anti-diabetic drug Liraglutide inhibits Zika Virus Infection by Suppressing AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis.
abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is a global health-threatening illness that causes severe neurological complications, including microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome. Currently, no approved antiviral therapeutics or vaccines are available for treating ZIKV infections. Using cell-based and mouse experiments, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist clinically used to treat diabetes by reducing hepatic glucose production, on viral replication, cell viability, and host metabolic signaling pathways. We found that liraglutide exhibited significant antiviral activity in a dose-dependent manner, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 5.5 ± 0.6 μM for viral RNA replication suppression, without cytotoxicity at the effective concentration. Furthermore, liraglutide treatment extended the lifespan of ZIKV-infected AG129 mice and achieved an approximately 15-fold reduction in viremia. Mechanistically, liraglutide enhanced 5' adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and then increased the phosphorylation of transducer of regulated CREB activity protein 2 (TORC2), thereby downregulating expression of rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzymes, specifically phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase and glucose-6-phosphatase. The antiviral activity of liraglutide was attenuated by both AMPK inhibitor Compound C and siRNA-mediated AMPK knockdown, supporting the claim that AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis contributes to liraglutide's anti-ZIKV activity. Given its clinical availability, liraglutide represents a promising therapeutic option for immediate repurposing for managing patients infected with ZIKV.

title: The NSUN2-ALYREF/YBX1-PTK7 axis drives hepatic stellate cell activation in liver fibrosis through m5C mRNA modification.
abstract: Liver fibrosis results from the overproduction and deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) from activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). NSUN2 is the main methyltransferase responsible for mRNA m5C modification. ALYREF and YBX1 are binding proteins recognizing m5C-modified mRNA. This study delineates the functional relevance of the NSUN2-m5C-ALYREF/YBX1 axis in HSC activation. NSUN2, ALYREF and YBX1, as well as m5C modification were detected in liver tissues from multiple fibrotic mouse models, in TGF-β1 stimulated LX-2 human HSCs and primary HSCs isolated from mice with immunohistochemistry, Western blot and immunofluorescent staining. The expression of NSUN2, ALYREF and YBX1 was inhibited using specific shRNAs or overexpressed in LX-2 cells to assess HSC activation markers by Western blot and cell motility by Transwell assay. m5C modification was evaluated using dot blot. m5C-modified genes regulated by NSUN2 were identified with m5C bisulfite sequencing and transcriptomic analysis. Potential genes regulated by NSUN2, ALYREF and YBX1 were identified with qPCR, RIP-qPCR, RNA stability assays, and functional validation. NSUN2, ALYREF and YBX1, as well as m5C modification increase in the liver tissues from high-fat diet (HFD) mice, carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) -treated mice, S. japonicum-infected mice and in activated HSCs. Inhibition of NSUN2, ALYREF and YBX1 suppresses HSC activation. NSUN2 promotes m5C modification and stabilizes PTK7 mRNA, thereby enhancing PTK7 protein expression and HSC activation. The regulation of PTK7 expression by NSUN2 depends on ALYREF and YBX1. NSUN2-ALYREF/YBX1-PTK7 axis drives HSC activation through m5C mRNA modification, which reveals a previously unrecognized epigenetic mechanism governing HSC biology.

title: A Sirtuin Protein FocSir2 Is Important for Oxidative Adaptation and Virulence of Banana Fusarium Wilt.
abstract: Banana Fusarium wilt, caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense tropical race 4 (Foc TR4), is a devastating disease of banana, but the molecular mechanism underlying its pathogenesis remains to be elucidated. In this study, we identified a sirtuin family protein, FocSir2, in Foc TR4. Global protein acetylation level was significantly increased in FocSIR2 knockout mutants compared with the wild type (WT), suggesting that FocSir2 is likely a deacetylase. FocSir2 was localized in the cytoplasm and was relatively highly expressed in conidia and during early infection. Deletion of FocSIR2 resulted in compact mycelial growth and a significant reduction in microconidium production, indicating a role for FocSIR2 in the asexual development of Foc TR4. The plate stress experiment indicates that FocSir2 plays important roles in cell wall integrity, osmotic stress, and pH stress responses. Notably, deletion of FocSIR2 led to greatly attenuated virulence toward banana corms and leaves, indicating that FocSir2 is essential for full virulence of Foc TR4. GO and KEGG analyses of differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq revealed enrichment in reactive oxygen species (ROS) metabolism and the TCA cycle. RT-qPCR confirmed that the expression of all eight ROS detoxification-related genes was reduced. The FocSIR2 knockout mutant was highly sensitive to H2O2 and exhibited an ROS burst during banana infection, indicating that FocSir2 is involved in the oxidative stress adaptation of Foc TR4 to the host. Further experiments demonstrated that deletion of FocSIR2 significantly decreased the activities of the TCA cycle key enzymes malate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, as well as the content of acetyl-CoA. Yeast library screening and yeast two-hybrid assays identified three proteins, FocRlc1, FOIG_08568, and FocFstf1, that interact with FocSir2, and their acetylation levels were significantly increased in the FocSIR2 knockout mutant, indicating that these three proteins are targets of FocSir2. Collectively, this study demonstrates that the deacetylase FocSir2 plays important roles in the asexual development and environmental stress responses of the pathogen and participates in the pathogenesis of the banana Fusarium wilt pathogen by regulating oxidative stress adaptation to the host.

title: Cysteine supplementation differentially regulates toxin production and macrophage responses in two Clostridioides difficile strains.
abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection is driven largely by toxin-mediated intestinal inflammation, and macrophages are among the first immune cells to respond to the pathogen. Whether cysteine-conditioned C. difficile differs in its interactions with macrophages across strains remains unclear. Two C. difficile strains (R20291 and CD12038) were cultured without (C0) or with 20 mM cysteine (C20), washed, and cocultured with RAW264.7 macrophages. Toxin expression and secretion, macrophage cytotoxicity, ROS, Annexin V-FITC/PI staining, inflammatory gene expression, and dual bacterial-host RNA-seq were analysed. In the CD12038 strain, cysE/cysK expression was higher in C0 than in C20 (P < 0.001), whereas tcdA/tcdB expression and supernatant TcdB concentrations were higher in C20 (P < 0.05); the R20291 strain showed the opposite pattern (P < 0.01). After coculture, the CD12038 C20 group caused more severe cytopathic effects, with greater LDH release (P = 0.007), higher ROS levels (P = 0.014), more Annexin V-FITC/PI-positive cells, and higher Il1b and Tnf-α mRNA expression (P < 0.05) than the C0 group; for R20291, the C0 group showed stronger cytotoxicity, greater ROS (P = 0.043), and higher Il1b/Tnf-α mRNA induction (both P < 0.05). Prokaryotic transcriptome analysis showed that CD12038 C20 was enriched in oxidoreductase activity and iron-sulfur cluster binding pathways, whereas R20291 C20 was enriched in protein folding, peptidase activity, and heat-stress response pathways. Host transcriptome analysis showed that pathways related to leukocyte migration, cytokine activity, the inflammatory response, and the immune response were enriched in cocultured macrophages, and R20291 C20 versus C0 was additionally enriched in myeloid leukocyte migration and cell population proliferation pathways. The two tested C. difficile strains responded in opposite directions to cysteine supplementation with respect to toxin production and RAW264.7 macrophage responses in vitro. These strain-pair-specific associations suggest that cysteine availability may modulate toxin production and host inflammatory gene expression in a strain-dependent manner.

title: Acetylated KLF5 as a therapeutic target mediating the anti-metastatic effects of doxycycline and methacycline in prostate cancer bone metastasis.
abstract: Bone metastasis is a common and lethal complication of breast, prostate, and lung cancers. TGF-β in the bone microenvironment is pivotal for metastatic progression. We previously demonstrated that TGF-β induces acetylation of KLF5 at K369 and that acetylated KLF5 (Ac-KLF5) drives epithelial-mesenchymal transition, invasiveness, and bone metastasis, positioning Ac-KLF5 and its effectors as therapeutic targets. Tetracycline derivatives, including doxycycline, show anti-metastatic activity, yet their molecular targets remain unidentified, limiting their clinical repurposing. Therapeutic development targeting Ac-KLF5 and elucidating targets of tetracycline derivatives are important areas of research in cancer therapy. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) screening of the FDA-approved drug library (1987 compounds) targeting purified KLF5K369Q (KQ, Ac-KLF5 mimic) protein identified candidates that bound to KQ, and the binding selectivities were verified by SPR and circular dichroism with wild-type KLF5 and acetylation-deficient KLF5K369R (KR) as controls. We assessed the anti-invasive activities of verified candidates in KQ-expressing prostate cancer cells using spheroid invasion and Transwell assays. In vivo therapeutic efficacy against bone metastasis was evaluated in tibial injection xenograft models using bioluminescence imaging, micro-CT, and histology. Mechanistic integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq, validated by qPCR, siRNA, and rescue experiments, elucidated downstream effectors and pathways. Doxycycline (D) and methacycline (M), but not their parent compound tetracycline (T), selectively bound to the KQ protein, with no binding to the KR acetylation-deficient KLF5 mutant. D and M, but not T, inhibited KQ-induced cell invasion, osteoclast differentiation, and osteolytic bone metastasis. RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analyses identified 22 genes whose transcription was regulated not only by KQ via direct promoter binding but also by D and M treatments. One of the genes, PGK1, was further confirmed to be responsible for D and M's suppressive effects in cell invasion, osteolytic differentiation, and bone metastasis. Doxycycline and methacycline are potential therapeutic agents for TGF-β-induced bone metastasis through selectively binding to Ac-KLF5.

title: Cry2 linked silkworm domestication to highly synchronized eclosion and rhythmic head transcriptomes.
abstract: Domestication often enhances the temporal synchronization of life-history events; yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the circadian basis of domestication-associated synchronization by comparing eclosion rhythms and circadian transcriptomes between the domesticated silkworm (Bombyx mori) and its wild ancestor (B. mandarina), and functionally dissected the role of the clock gene Cry2. Under 14:10 light-dark cycles, both species exhibited significant daily eclosion rhythms; however, B. mori showed markedly higher synchronization and a distinct phase advance, resulting in a sharply clustered early-morning peak compared with the broader afternoon pattern in B. mandarina. Cry2 knockout did not substantially affect eclosion timing under LD cycles, but under constant darkness it delayed phase, reduced robustness and synchronization of the eclosion rhythm, suggesting that Cry2 promotes the precision and synchrony of endogenous eclosion rhythms. To uncover transcriptional signatures of domestication, we performed 24-h RNA-seq on heads of domestic, wild, and Cry2-mutant silkworms. Thousands of rhythmic genes and broad oscillatory expression of core clock genes were detected in B. mori, whereas only dozens of rhythmic transcripts were found in B. mandarina. Disruption of Cry2 strongly reduced the detectable domestication-expanded rhythmic transcriptional program, reducing the number of rhythmic genes from thousands to fewer than one hundred. Rhythmic outputs in B. mori were enriched in protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum, Toll/Imd signaling, and daytime-biased tyrosine metabolism/dopamine biosynthesis pathways. Co-expression network analysis further revealed that domestication strengthened clock-linked regulatory networks, which became fragmented in both the Cry2 mutant and wild silkworms. These findings demonstrate that domestication promotes interindividual synchronization of eclosion by expanding and coordinating circadian transcriptional programs, suggesting that Cry2 acts as a potential candidate gene contributing to this adaptive rhythmic network.

title: Machine Learning-based Transcriptomic Data Analysis of Long COVID Patients: Generating Hypotheses for Molecular Signatures
abstract: Introduction: Long COVID (LC) remains a global public-health challenge, affecting an estimated 10-30% of COVID-19-survivors. Machine learning (ML) can help identify molecular features associated with LC. Human ion channels (HICs), that regulate immune-cell signaling and cellular homeostasis, may contribute to LC-associated processes and offer insights into relevant pathways and potential drug-repurposing candidates. Methodology: RNA-seq data from COVID-19-recovered and LC patients across six datasets were integrated, preprocessed, and corrected for batch effects. Supervised ML models were evaluated using leave-one-batch-out validation, with SHAP identifying features across validation folds. Functional enrichment, host-host and host-viral protein-protein interaction analyses were performed, followed by drug interaction analysis of potential HICs within the resulting interactome. Results: A support vector classifier with an RBF kernel achieved a mean-AUC of 0.664 across six validation folds. SHAP analysis of the three selected folds (AUC = 0.722, 0.836, and 0.817) identified 225, 153, and 241 genes, respectively. Functional enrichment highlighted pathways including histidine metabolism and TNF signaling. Among the 613 genes identified across these folds, 9 were HICs and 39 were immune signaling-related genes (ISGs), whose protein-protein interaction analysis revealed a pharmacologically relevant interactome. Furthermore, four HICs including CLCN3, KCNQ3, RYR1, and ZACN interacted with 30 approved drugs. Conclusion: ML-based analysis of integrated RNA-seq data identified HICs and ISGs associated with LC, while functional enrichment and PPI analyses provided insights into their potential biological relevance. Drug interaction analysis further highlighted candidate HIC-targeting drugs for future investigation in LC management. This computational framework provides preliminary, hypothesis-generating insights to guide future research.

title: Generating scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq using a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder.
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides detailed, genome-wide gene expression profiles at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of disease-driving cell types and genes. However, scRNA-seq remains costly, and there are extremely limited samples generated in even the most extensive human disease studies. In contrast, bulk RNA-seq data is abundant but averages gene expression across all cell types, losing cell-specific detail. To further leverage this abundance of RNA-seq data, methods have been developed to infer cell type proportions and average expression from bulk data using scRNA-seq as a reference. Additionally, generative AI models have been developed to generate more of an existing scRNA-seq dataset, spatial transcriptome data from bulk, and a complete single-cell dataset from bulk, with an incomplete set of single-cell data, for large cohort studies. However, there is a lack of tools specifically dedicated to generating representative single-cell RNA-seq from bulk RNA-seq data. To address this, we develop an innovative, modular framework, termed Bulk2SC, that takes full advantage of powerful generative AI approaches and existing scRNA-seq data to generate representative scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq. Bulk2SC uses a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder for data generation together with any tool that predicts cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq data. We demonstrate the superior performance of Bulk2SC relative to tools that generate scRNA-seq from bulk RNA-seq as part of broader computational frameworks on published datasets from multiple tissue types. We also apply and assess Bulk2SC on a benchmark deconvolution dataset that contains paired bulk and single nucleus RNA-seq data. The modular design of Bulk2SC allows for deconvolution of single datasets as well as straightforward implementation within larger computational frameworks.

title: Integrated Transcriptomics Defines a Conserved Three-Dimensional Priming Program in Umbilical Cord and Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells for Liver-Directed Therapy.
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) and extracellular-matrix-supported culture can enhance mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapeutic activity, but transcriptional programs conserved across MSC sources and liver-mimicking formats remain incompletely defined. To determine how three-dimensional culture reshapes MSC state and liver-regenerative competence across cell sources and culture formats, and to separate the contribution of cell aggregation from that of a surrounding matrix. Three bulk RNA-sequencing datasets comparing three-dimensional with two-dimensional culture were integrated across umbilical cord-derived MSCs and bone marrow-derived MSCs. Formats comprised spheroids, self-assembled cell-and-matrix complexes, and a ceramic-scaffold niche model. One dataset profiles a spheroid and a cell-and-matrix complex against the same two-dimensional baseline, which separates aggregation from matrix within a single matched design. Differential expression, gene set enrichment, cross-dataset concordance, and program scoring were used to resolve immunomodulation, fibrosis-related remodeling, proliferation, senescence, and hepatic competence. Three-dimensional culture induced a conserved cross-source transcriptional program characterized by nuclear factor kappa B-associated inflammatory licensing and increased soluble immunomodulatory mediators, including TSG-6, prostaglandin E2-related enzymes, STC1, and interleukin-6-family factors. MSCs also shifted from a contractile myofibroblast-like state toward a matrix-remodeling phenotype, with reduced ACTA2, TAGLN, CCN2, THBS1, LOX, and SERPINE1 and increased MMP1 and MMP3. Aggregation alone reproduced the direction and identity of the matrix-format response, which agreed at a Spearman correlation of 0.89 with 98% of co-significant genes moving the same way, and the matrix scaled the same axis rather than engaging a different one. Cell-cycle and DNA-replication programs were suppressed without coordinated induction of canonical senescence effectors, supporting quiescence rather than senescence. Hepatic-competence programs were primed, whereas ALB, CYP enzymes, HNF4A, and HNF1A remained low or absent, indicating priming without hepatocyte conversion. Integrated transcriptomics identifies a conserved three-dimensional MSC state coupling immunomodulatory secretion, matrix remodeling, proliferative quiescence, and subthreshold hepatic competence, and shows that cell aggregation alone establishes its direction and identity, with a surrounding matrix adding amplitude rather than new content. These findings provide a transcriptomic framework for designing scalable MSC culture systems and for developing candidate potency markers, which remain to be tested against functional assays.

title: A Nitrated T-Cell Epitope Enhances the Antitumor Immune Response of a TOPK-Targeted Vaccine in Glioblastoma and Its Potential for Remodeling the Tumor Microenvironment.
abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains the most lethal primary brain tumor in adults, largely due to recurrence after surgery. Cancer vaccines, which can activate a patient's adaptive immune system against specific tumor antigens, are a promising strategy for improving outcomes in patients with GBM. Methods: We examined the function of T-lymphokine-activated killer cell-originated protein kinase (TOPK), a candidate tumor-associated antigen, in GBM. We then constructed TOPK-NitraTh, a vaccine coupled to a nitrated T-cell epitope (NitraTh) and targeting TOPK. Its efficacy was evaluated in the GL261 orthotopic GBM model, and single-cell RNA sequencing was used to explore the underlying immune mechanisms. Results: TOPK functioned as a tumor-promoting factor in GBM. Vaccination with TOPK-NitraTh elicited TOPK-specific adaptive immune responses and inhibited GBM progression in the GL261 orthotopic model. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing analysis led us to hypothesize that the NitraTh-based vaccine may reprogram macrophages potentially via the NF-κB signaling pathway, potentially contributing to the reversal of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Conclusions: Given its ability to remodel the tumor microenvironment, the NitraTh-based vaccine represents a promising preclinical strategy for GBM treatment.

title: The mechanism of chemotherapy resistance induced by Fusobacterium nucleatum in colorectal cancer through upregulation of ATF3 expression.
abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum) is frequently enriched in colorectal cancer (CRC) and implicated in poor chemotherapy response, but the host factors linking infection to chemoresistance remain incompletely defined. We investigated the effect of F. nucleatum on CRC cell responses to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and irinotecan. Using the GEO RNA-sequencing data set GSE90944 of F. nucleatum-treated CRC cells, we identified F. nucleatum-responsive host genes. Bioinformatic prioritization highlighted activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) as a candidate involved in F. nucleatum-associated chemoresistance. qPCR and Western blot analyses confirmed increased ATF3 mRNA and protein levels in F. nucleatum-infected CRC cells. F. nucleatum infection attenuated the cytotoxic effects of 5-FU and irinotecan in CRC cells. In vitro functional assays showed differences between infected and uninfected cells in relative proliferation, wound closure, cell-cycle distribution, and apoptosis under chemotherapy conditions. During treatment with either 5-FU or irinotecan, ATF3 knockdown was associated with more pronounced changes in relative cell viability and apoptosis under F. nucleatum-infected conditions, whereas ATF3 rescue partially reversed these changes. Additional interaction analyses provided statistical evidence for infection-associated differences in normalized 5-FU responses, with more robust support in HCT116 cells. In a nude mouse xenograft model, F. nucleatum infection attenuated the antitumor effects of both 5-FU and irinotecan, whereas ATF3 knockdown was associated with reduced tumor burden under F. nucleatum-infected chemotherapy conditions. Together, these findings support ATF3 as a functional host factor in F. nucleatum-associated chemotherapy responses and warrant further investigation of the F. nucleatum-ATF3 axis as a potential therapeutic target in CRC. Chemotherapy resistance limits colorectal cancer treatment. Fusobacterium nucleatum is enriched in colorectal cancer and associated with poor treatment response, but the host factors involved remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that Fusobacterium nucleatum reduces colorectal cancer cell sensitivity to 5-fluorouracil and irinotecan and induces activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3). During treatment with 5-fluorouracil or irinotecan, ATF3 depletion produced more pronounced changes in cell viability and apoptosis under Fusobacterium nucleatum-infected conditions, whereas ATF3 rescue partially reversed these effects. In a xenograft model, ATF3 knockdown was associated with reduced tumor burden under F. nucleatum-infected chemotherapy conditions. These findings identify an inducible host factor contributing to Fusobacterium nucleatum-associated chemoresistance and provide a rationale for further investigation of this host-microbe interaction as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Sublethal rifampicin enhances the tolerance of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus to food processing and intestinal retention through protein aggregation.
abstract: Lactic acid bacteria in fermented foods and the human gut are chronically exposed to environmental stressors that can trigger adaptive responses. Bacterial dormancy allows non-spore-forming bacteria to withstand adverse conditions through a metabolically suppressed, reversible state. This study aimed to investigate whether sublethal antibiotic stress unexpectedly triggers adaptive responses in Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus, a widely used probiotic and starter culture, and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and functional consequences. Sublethal rifampicin-induced a dormant state in Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus sp1.1, characterized by reduced ATP levels and impaired cell division, with colony recovery upon stress removal. This state enhanced cross-tolerance to acid, alkali, and heat stress, prolonged intestinal retention in mice, and increased the impact on gut microbial community structure. Disruption of protein aggregates by pH adjustment or 1,6-hexanediol treatment abolished the enhanced tolerance. Rifampicin triggered a metabolic shift toward transcriptional and translational inhibition. Protein aggregates selectively enriched translation, RNA metabolism, and DNA repair proteins. Two disordered proteins, Gene1622 and Gene1909, were upregulated in whole cell and enriched in the aggregates. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified a cluster that sustained alaS and gatA expression under global translational suppression, contrasting with their downregulation in bulk RNA-seq, revealing population heterogeneity under stress. Our results support a model in which protein aggregates function as "molecular safe houses" that sequester and protect translation-and DNA-repair-related proteins, thereby locally enhancing the efficiency of key protein translation and DNA repair while also serving as a protein reservoir for subsequent growth recovery. This reversible dormancy provides a theoretical basis for engineering robust starter cultures, while also raising ecological considerations regarding stress-induced adaptation in the food chain, including potential impacts on gut microbial homeostasis. Video Abstract.

title: Hsp20-Promoted Protective Protein Aggregation Drives Stress Tolerance Heterogeneity in Bacteria.
abstract: Phenotypic heterogeneity in stress tolerance among isogenic bacterial cells fundamentally impacts the efficiency and robustness of microbial bioprocesses while fostering persistent infections, yet its underlying regulatory mechanisms remain elusive. Here, by integrating single-cell RNA-sequencing with microfluidic time-lapse tracking, we discovered small heat shock protein Hsp20 as a central regulator of acid-tolerance heterogeneity. Strikingly, contrary to its canonical role as a holdase to prevent protein aggregation, Hsp20 actively promotes the formation of protective protein aggregates that sequester transcription and metabolic proteins to inactivate gene transcription and metabolism. Hsp20-promoted aggregates drive cells into varying depths of dormancy, regulating the trade-off between stress tolerance and post-stress recovery of single cells. Hsp20 enhances cellular tolerance at the expense of recovery capacity, an aspect that has rarely been systematically reported. Moreover, Hsp20-regulated protection extends broadly to heat, oxidative, and bile salt stresses, revealing a generalizable strategy for stress adaptation. Our work broadens the roles of small heat shock proteins in cytoplasmic protective aggregation during the microbial stress response and provides a mechanistic link between transcriptional noise and phenotypic heterogeneity. It offers a new theoretical basis for understanding the survival strategies of prokaryotes and for precision control in microbial industry and epidemic control.

title: Multi-omics integration identifies COQ8A in excitatory neurons as a protective gene in major depressive disorder.
abstract: The pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD) remains insufficiently understood, which may be due to the limitations of bulk tissue analyses in addressing cellular heterogeneity. In this study, we applied a comprehensive approach combining brain cell-type-specific expression quantitative trait loci data, MDD genome-wide association study summary statistics, and MDD single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data, with the aim of identifying cell-specific key genes. The utilization of summary-based mendelian randomization and two-sample mendelian randomization analyses resulted in the discovery of 26 candidate genes, of which 15 exhibited strong colocalization signals across four distinct brain cell types. Combining snRNA-seq data analysis, we discovered that COQ8A is down-regulated in excitatory neurons (Ex) and LATS1 is up-regulated in oligodendrocytes in MDD patients. These findings were further validated by mice chronic social defeat stress models, which demonstrated significant downregulation of COQ8A in Ex of prefrontal cortex (PFC). Functional analysis suggests a relationship between the down-regulated expression of COQ8A in Ex from the MDD group and impaired energy metabolism, mitochondrial function, and protein synthesis. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicated that eight antidepressants bind to COQ8A with high affinity, with Escitalopram and Paroxetine effectively stabilizing its active sites. Our findings indicate that COQ8A in Ex of the PFC, associated with mitochondrial function, may serve as a key protective gene in MDD. Furthermore, COQ8A emerges as a promising therapeutic target for precision antidepressant treatment. This study enhances our understanding of the neurobiological basis of MDD at the single-cell level.

title: Beyond Amyloid in Alzheimer's Disease: A Multiscale Evidence-Based Review of Pathogenesis, Biomarkers, and Emerging Therapeutics.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterised neuropathologically by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, phosphorylated-tau neurofibrillary tangles, synaptic dysfunction, and neuronal loss. However, the temporal and causal relationships underlying disease initiation, progression, and clinical heterogeneity remain incompletely resolved. Increasing evidence supports a multiscale model in which amyloid-tau pathology intersects with genetic susceptibility, epigenetic regulation, impaired proteostasis, mitochondrial and metabolic stress, neuroimmune activation, vascular dysfunction, and declining neural resilience. Familial variants in APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 directly perturb amyloid processing, whereas APOE ε4, TREM2, and polygenic variation influence lipid metabolism, protein clearance, vascular integrity, and glial responses. DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, and non-coding RNAs may further shape neuronal and immune states, although their directionality and causal significance remain incompletely established. Similarly, microbial and environmental exposures have been associated with inflammatory and proteostatic alterations, but definitive evidence for causation in sporadic AD is lacking. This review integrates genetic, epigenetic, proteostatic, metabolic, neuroimmune, vascular, and environmental mechanisms across disease stages and cellular compartments. We critically evaluate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma biomarkers, amyloid/tau PET, multimodal imaging, extracellular vesicles, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled approaches for diagnosis, prognosis, stratification, and therapeutic prioritisation. Therapeutic evidence is stratified from established symptomatic treatments and approved anti-amyloid antibodies to investigational tau-, immune-, epigenetic-, RNA-, microbiome-, stem-cell-, neuromodulatory-, and nanoparticle-based strategies. By distinguishing causal human evidence from observational, experimental, and computational findings, this synthesis identifies priorities for biomarker-guided, stage-specific, and mechanism-informed interventions while avoiding premature inference of causality or clinical benefit.

title: Decoding immune signatures driving brain metastases in stage III non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Development of brain metastasis (BM) during follow-up remains challenging in radically treated stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC). Characterizing the molecular and immunological landscape of primary tumors may provide insight into factors associated with subsequent BM development. We performed comparative targeted gene expression profiles in primary tumors from patients with radically treated stage III NSCLC who developed BM versus those with other organ metastases (OOM). Exploratory analysis of two prospective studies (NVALT-11 [NCT01282437], NL3335) and one retrospective series including patients with adequately staged and radically treated stage III NSCLC. Available baseline FFPE biopsies of the primary (stage III NSCLC diagnosis) were collected. PanCancer IO 360™ Panel was utilized to measure gene expression profiles. Targeted gene expression analysis was performed using NanoString Technology. In-depth multiplex protein spatial measurements in independent NSCLC samples (BM = 6 and OOM = 10) was performed using GeoMx™ Digital Spatial Profiler (DSP) profiling. Tissue samples of 208/636 patients were evaluated (excluded: n = 329 non-primary samples and n = 99 tissue unavailable). Additionally, 166 samples were excluded because of insufficient RNA, and 1 sample was excluded because it was a duplicate. A total of 41 samples were included (11 BM, 30 OOM). We revealed elevated expression of a mast cell gene-signature in the primary of the BM-development group. With DSP profiling we identified higher expression of CD14, FOXP3, and BCL-2 proteins within tumor infiltrated regions of the BM group. These findings identify immune features of primary NSCLC associated with subsequent BM development and warrant validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: The circSRSF5-FUS-EIF4A3 regulatory circuitry protects Ewing sarcoma cells from EWS::FLI1 small-molecule inhibition.
abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of circSRSF5. Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for circSRSF5 in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly circSRSF5, in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.

title: Thymol attenuates bleomycin‑induced pulmonary fibrosis in mice by regulating the E2F8/NF‑κB/TGF‑β1/smad signaling pathway.
abstract: To investigate the potential therapeutic effect of thymol on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) by regulating the E2F8/NF‑κB/TGF‑β1/Smad signaling pathway. A CCK-8 assay was employed to determine the non-toxic concentration range of thymol. Human lung fibroblasts (HFL1 cells) were divided into four groups: Control, TGF-β1-induced, Thymol (80 μM) + TGF-β1, and Thymol (160 μM) + TGF-β1. The mRNA and protein expression levels of α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), Collagen I, and Fibronectin were assessed by RT-qPCR and Western blotting. A bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis was established and divided into five groups: Control, BLM-induced, Thymol (60 mg/kg), Thymol (120 mg/kg), and Nintedanib (100 mg/kg). Survival rate, body weight, and inflammatory indices were recorded. Lung inflammation and fibrosis were evaluated using hematoxylin and eosin (HE) and Masson's trichrome staining. Transcriptome‑wide RNA‑seq analysis was performed to characterize global transcriptional reprogramming induced by TGF‑β1 and thymol, including principal component analysis, differential‑gene screening, and Gene Ontology enrichment analysis. Differentially expressed genes were screened by RNA-seq, and expression levels of E2F8 and components of the NF-κB/TGF-β1/Smad pathway were validated by RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Thymol at concentrations up to 160 μM exhibited no significant cytotoxicity toward normal human lung fibroblasts. Thymol below 160 μM significantly inhibited TGF-β1-induced proliferation of fibroblasts (P < 0.05). Compared to the control group, the TGF-β1-induced group exhibited increased mRNA and protein levels of α-SMA, Collagen I, and Fibronectin, as well as enhanced phosphorylation of p65, Smad2, and Smad3, and elevated E2F8 mRNA expression (P < 0.05). These changes were significantly suppressed in both the Thymol (80 μM) + TGF-β1 and Thymol (160 μM) + TGF-β1 groups (P < 0.05), except for Collagen I, which remained unaffected. Transcriptomic data revealed that thymol only partially reversed TGF‑β1‑triggered transcriptional alterations, preferentially suppressing myofibroblast‑contractile gene programs rather than broadly abrogating all extracellular‑matrix‑related transcripts. In vivo, the BLM group showed significant increases in TGF-β1 levels, white blood cell, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts, as well as in alveolar inflammation and fibrosis scores, compared to the control group. These parameters were significantly reduced in the thymol-treated groups (P < 0.05). This study demonstrates that thymol can suppress fibroblast proliferation and activation by regulating the E2F8/NF‑κB/TGF‑β1/Smad signaling axis, and thymol exerts selective partial transcriptional reprogramming thereby alleviating inflammation and pulmonary fibrosis in mice. These findings provide a foundational basis for further exploration of thymol as a candidate antifibrotic agent in IPF therapy.

title: Association of the peripheral-blood tristetraprolin-to-HuR messenger RNA ratio with the severity of lung involvement in COVID-19: an exploratory cross-sectional study.
abstract: Host cytokine dysregulation is a major driver of COVID-19 severity. Cytokine and inflammatory transcripts bearing AU-rich elements are post-transcriptionally controlled by two antagonistic RNA-binding proteins: HuR (ELAVL1), which stabilizes them, and tristetraprolin (TTP; ZFP36), which promotes their decay. In this cross-sectional study, 83 patients with RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 (Fasa, Iran; August 2023-January 2024) were sampled at diagnosis, before treatment; patients with comorbidities, medication use or vaccination within six months were excluded. Peripheral-blood HuR, TTP and β-actin transcripts were quantified by SYBR Green RT-qPCR (2^-ΔΔCt method, calibrated to the mild-involvement group), and a TTP/HuR ratio was derived. Lung involvement on chest imaging was mild in 40 patients (48.2%), moderate in 24 (28.9%) and severe in 19 (22.9%); six patients (7.2%) died. HuR rose and the ratio fell across severity strata (both p < 0.001), mainly between mild and moderate disease, whereas TTP did not differ (p = 0.148). The ratio discriminated moderate or severe from mild involvement (AUC 0.78, 95% CI 0.68-0.88), although not better than HuR alone, and remained associated with severity after adjustment for age, sex and smoking (ordinal odds ratio per doubling 0.59, 95% CI 0.46-0.75). It was lower in non-survivors (0.331 vs. 0.948; p = 0.041), but this association rested on six deaths and was not robust to adjustment (p = 0.106). The TTP/HuR mRNA ratio showed a consistent inverse association with COVID-19 severity and a weaker, exploratory association with mortality. Larger multicenter studies with protein-level data and independent validation are needed before any biomarker use. Not applicable. This study was observational and was not a clinical trial.

title: Cytokine-Driven Immunomodulatory Heterogeneity of Epicardial Adipose Tissue-Derived Stromal Cells Under Simulated Ischemia-Reperfusion.
abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue-derived stem cells (EATDS) modulate post-infarction remodeling through paracrine signaling whereas the cytokine-specific responses and EATDS sub-populations under ischemia and reperfusion remain poorly defined. We hypothesize that differential expression of cytokines drives distinct sub-phenotypes of EATDS. Our objective is to assess the expression level of major cytokines, TGF-β1, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-17, and IL-18, associated with myocardial injury under simulated ischemic/reperfused EATDS. We aim to decipher the sub-phenotypes based on cytokine-associated transcriptional signatures at single-cell resolution. Swine EATDS were cultured under Control, ischemia (ISC), and ischemia/reperfusion (ISC/R) conditions. Expression of the above cytokines was measured using qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and Western blotting. Single-cell RNA sequencing and network analysis were used to define phenotype-specific transcriptional programs and enriched pathways. IL-6 exhibited sustained activation at both transcript and protein levels during ISC and ISC/R, whereas TGF-β1 showed sustained protein-level expression across conditions. In contrast, TNF-α and IL-17 displayed phase-restricted or transcriptionally uncoupled patterns, while IL-1β and IL-18 demonstrated persistent transcriptional induction with discordant protein-level responses. Single-cell analysis identified proliferating and stromal EATDS as the most responsive subsets, demonstrating stress-adaptive and extracellular remodeling signatures, including MMP3 and HSP90B1 upregulation. EATDS displayed heterogeneous cytokine responses to ischemia and reperfusion, with proliferating and stromal subsets showing pronounced transcriptional remodeling, while activated fibroblast and smooth muscle cells exhibited comparatively attenuated cytokine responsiveness. Overall, the findings provide a framework for future multimodal studies for refining EATDS sub-phenotypes to modulate post-ischemic inflammation and repair.

title: Extracellular vesicle-derived LINC02313 stabilizes HNRNPC to drive PKM2-dependent glycolytic reprogramming and proliferation in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Increasing evidence highlights the critical roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in tumor initiation and progression, particularly in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate intercellular communication by transferring functional cargos, including lncRNAs. However, the biological significance of tumor-derived EV-enriched lncRNAs in HCC remains poorly understood. EV-associated lncRNAs were identified through integrative analyses of the TCGA-LIHC and exoRBase datasets. LINC02313 expression was validated in HCC tissues and serum-derived EVs. EVs were isolated and characterized by TEM, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and EV marker profiling. Gain- and loss-of-function assays, together with CCK-8, colony formation, xenograft, and metabolic analyses, were performed to assess the effects of LINC02313 on HCC proliferation and glycolysis. RNA-seq was used to explore downstream pathways. The interaction between LINC02313 and HNRNPC was examined by RNA pulldown, RIP-qPCR, protein stability, ubiquitination, and domain-mapping assays. PKM alternative splicing was assessed by qPCR, Western blotting, and modulation of m6A signaling. Here, we identified LINC02313 as an HCC-derived, EV-associated lncRNA through integrative analysis of public datasets and found that it was markedly upregulated in both HCC tissues and serum-derived EVs from patients with HCC. Further analyses showed that EV-delivered LINC02313 could be efficiently transferred into recipient HCC cells, where it promoted malignant progression. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that LINC02313 enhanced HCC cell proliferation and glycolytic activity. Mechanistically, LINC02313 bound to the RNA recognition motif (RRM) domain of HNRNPC through its S2 region, thereby stabilizing HNRNPC protein by preventing its ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation. Further investigation identified BTRC as an E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in HNRNPC ubiquitination and degradation, while LINC02313 disrupted the interaction between BTRC and HNRNPC rather than directly binding to BTRC. Stabilized HNRNPC, in turn, promoted METTL3-mediated modulation of PKM alternative splicing, leading to PKM2 upregulation, enhanced aerobic glycolysis, and increased HCC cell proliferation and tumor progression. EV-derived LINC02313 promotes glycolytic reprogramming and accelerates HCC progression by stabilizing HNRNPC, thereby facilitating PKM2 upregulation. These findings elucidate a previously unrecognized oncogenic mechanism of EV-mediated lncRNA signaling in HCC and identify LINC02313 as a candidate non-invasive biomarker for HCC detection.

title: Cell-Type-Specific Expression Is Hard to Predict from Bulk, but It Is Still Useful
abstract: Single-cell-informed deconvolution provides cell-type-resolved features for clinical bulk RNA cohorts. Most existing methods predict the proportions $π_k$ of the $K$ constituent cell types (CTs). Fewer predict cell-type-specific expression (CTSE) $μ_{kg}$ of gene $g$ in CT $k$, which can capture cell states that proportions miss, but recent benchmarks find it much harder. We explain this gap with closed-form accuracy bounds. For CTSE, we derive an $R^2$ ceiling for per-gene linear estimators. For proportions, the best linear estimator, which pools evidence across genes, has a closed-form $R^2$, and a computable lower bound on it predicts which CTs are learnable. We study targeted deconvolution of 106 biologically curated (CT, gene) pairs, found post hoc to have higher learnability scores. On overall survival in non-small cell lung cancer, estimation difficulty does not predict prognostic value across these targets. Yet a sparse survival model on deconvolved features, mostly CTSE, predicts survival as well as a sparse model on the bulk genes themselves, while attributing its signal to specific cell types. Some deconvolved CTSE features reveal prognostic signal not seen in the corresponding bulk gene.

title: Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome in People Living with HIV on Antiretroviral Therapy-Insights from a Ten-Year Retrospective Analysis in a Romanian Tertiary Hospital.
abstract: Initiation of effective antiretroviral therapy (ART) in people living with HIV (PLWH) may lead to the development of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). Characteristics of unmasking versus paradoxical IRIS, and the impact of ART regimens remain incompletely characterized in real-world cohorts. We conducted a single-center retrospective analysis of patients diagnosed with IRIS over the period 2015-2025 in a tertiary-care hospital of Infectious Diseases from Bucharest, Romania. Several clinical and biological variables were comparatively analyzed between patients with unmasking versus paradoxical IRIS, and between those receiving integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTI)-based versus non-INSTI regimens. A total of 57 PLWH were included. The median time to IRIS onset was 21 days [IQR = 14]. Unmasking IRIS was diagnosed in 43.9% of cases, while 56.1% of patients developed paradoxical IRIS. Median values of CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell count, CD4/CD8 ratio, HIV RNA, fibrinogen and C-reactive protein prior ART and upon IRIS diagnosis did not significantly vary according to the IRIS subtype and the ART regimen. However, trends in clinical manifestations and paraclinical parameters highlight the heterogeneity of IRIS presentations. Paired analyses showed increases in CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts, CD4/CD8 ratio, fibrinogen and CRP, and a decline in HIV RNA (all p < 0.01). Mortality due to IRIS-related complications was 14.0% overall (24.0% in unmasking IRIS versus 6.3% in paradoxical IRIS; two-sided Fisher's exact p = 0.120). INSTI use was not significantly associated with IRIS subtype after adjustment for baseline CD4+ T-cell count and time since HIV diagnosis (aOR 0.54, 95% CI 0.14-2.09). This analysis provides insights into the clinical and biological profiles of IRIS and provides valuable descriptive data in clinical practice. Rapid CD4+ T-cell count recovery and HIV RNA decline in presence of elevated inflammatory biomarkers suggest IRIS, but most immunological and virological parameters did not differ significantly by IRIS subtype or ART regimen. Our findings emphasize IRIS variability in clinical cohorts and the importance of further studies to identify more reliable predictive markers for IRIS.

title: Pathway-Transformer: Integrating Transcript Variants and Biological Pathways for Cancer Phenotype Prediction.
abstract: Understanding the biological functions and regulatory mechanisms that shape cancer outcomes is critical for explaining cancer progression and guiding targeted therapies. Integrative analysis of multi-omics data has become widely used to provide a more complete molecular view of cancer. However, many phenotype changes driven by protein abnormalities arise from upstream regulatory processes, and existing methods often ignore transcript variants generated by post-transcriptional events such as alternative splicing and alternative polyadenylation. To address this limitation, we propose Pathway-Transformer, a computational framework that integrates transcript variants and gene expression derived from the same RNA-seq data to predict cancer phenotypes using biological pathways as prior knowledge. Pathway-Transformer encodes the structural properties of pathway networks and uses a transformer encoder to learn pathway-specific representations of transcriptional regulation, which are then aggregated across pathways for phenotype prediction. We evaluate Pathway-Transformer on TCGA breast cancer patient samples using multiple cancer-related KEGG pathways. Results from both individual pathways and integrated pathway sets consistently show that transcript variants derived from alternative splicing and alternative polyadenylation provide more informative molecular signatures and lead to improved clinical outcome prediction compared with gene expression profiles alone. Applying the same experimental setup to the METABRIC breast cancer cohort yields comparable performance for cancer status prediction, indicating that the framework is not specific to a single cohort. In addition, analysis of the highest performing pathways and of attention scores computed from the learned parameters identified biologically relevant hormone receptor and signaling programs, supporting the interpretability of the proposed framework. Source code is available at: https://github.com/compbiolabucf/PathwayTransformer.

title: oddSNP: a predictive framework for optimizing multiplexed single-cell RNA-seq experiments.
abstract: Donor multiplexing is a powerful strategy to increase scale, lower the costs, and reduce batch effects in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq), but clear guidelines for experimental design are lacking, forcing researchers to risk costly demultiplexing failures. We introduce SNP-Information Content (SNP-IC), a quantitative metric computable from simple unpooled pilot data that accurately predicts the success of genotype-based demultiplexing. Across multiple large-scale datasets using stem cell and organoid models, we establish a robust SNP-IC threshold of approximately 50, above which cells can be reliably assigned to their donor of origin. For more challenging genotype-free approaches, we define a pairwise metric, cpSNP-IC, and demonstrate a much higher requirement of approximately 3000. Our open-source framework, oddSNP, implements this predictive model to enable in-silico titration of sequencing depth and donor complexity, allowing researchers to optimize study design before large-scale deployment, while managing costs and minimizing the risk of catastrophic data loss. oddSNP can be installed directly from PyPI and Bioconda. Source code is also freely available from GitHub at https://www.github.com/nemoto-lab/oddSNP (with release versions also available in Zenodo at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19378022). Novel scRNAseq data used as part of this study is available at the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) website under accession GSE334633.

title: ETS1 as a Candidate Biomarker for Sepsis‑Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Multi‑Omics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
