abstract: This multi‑omics study aimed to screen candidate molecules associated with the transition from sepsis to sepsis‑associated ARDS, and provide preliminary biological evidence for risk‑stratification research. Public transcriptomic datasets were used for differential‑gene analysis, WGCNA, lung‑tissue‑expression filtering and multi‑algorithm machine‑learning screening. We performed transcriptome sequencing on peripheral blood samples from our exploratory single‑center cohort including 22 sepsis patients and 10 healthy volunteers to verify gene dysregulation in sepsis vs healthy status. Associations between gene expression and established ARDS among sepsis patients were assessed using the public dataset GSE32707 only. Single‑cell RNA‑seq data, functional enrichment and literature mining were applied to explore potential molecular mechanisms. Twenty‑seven candidate genes related to septic lung injury were obtained. ETS1 emerged as a hub gene with high model contribution across machine‑learning and SHAP interpretability analyses. In our clinical cohort, ETS1 was significantly down‑regulated in sepsis patients compared with healthy controls. Analysis of the public GSE32707 dataset further suggested that ETS1 exhibited stepwise reduction from healthy controls, through uncomplicated sepsis, to sepsis complicated with ARDS. Single‑cell analysis demonstrated that ETS1 was predominantly expressed in NK cells, T cells and B‑cells, implying potential roles in immune‑homeostasis regulation. Our machine‑learning models achieved high classification performance for discriminating sepsis from healthy volunteers. However, this classification task cannot directly predict incident ARDS among sepsis patients. In this hypothesis‑generating observational multi‑omics study, reduced ETS1 expression was correlated with sepsis and further decreased in patients with established sepsis‑associated ARDS in one public dataset. ETS1 represents a candidate correlative biomarker for sepsis risk stratification. Further large multi‑center cohorts, cell‑composition correction and functional wet‑lab experiments are required to validate whether ETS1 can support ARDS early‑warning or serve as a therapeutic target for septic lung injury.

title: Interpretable Blood Transcriptomic Classification of Ebola Survivors: A Machine Learning Framework for Post-Recovery Immune Profiling.
abstract: Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors may experience persistent immune dysfunction and inflammatory complications after recovery, highlighting the need for blood-based approaches to characterize post-Ebola biological changes. We investigated whether whole-blood transcriptomics could distinguish EVD survivors (EVD-Ss) from healthy controls and identify candidate transcriptional features associated with survivor status. Public whole-blood RNA-sequencing data from 26 EVD-Ss and 33 healthy donors from the same geographical region in Guinea [Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO): GSE143549] were analyzed using DESeq2 for differential expression. An elastic-net logistic regression classifier underwent nested cross-validation (5 outer, 3 inner folds), with gene ranking, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning restricted exclusively to training splits. Performance was assessed using 100 repeated partitions and a full-pipeline permutation test (1,000 permutations). Gene-selection stability was evaluated across 500 cross-validation fits and 200 subsamples, with comparisons against principal-component-only, cell-composition-only, and sex-only models. The classifier achieved a pooled out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.962 [95% DeLong confidence interval (CI): 0.917 to 1.000] and mean repeated-cross-validation AUC of 0.960 (95% subject-bootstrap CI: 0.926 to 0.987). Gene selection varied from 1 to 50 genes across resampled fits; a principal-component-only model showed comparable discrimination. Candidate genes require further validation of reproducibility and biological relevance and represent an exploratory, unstable set rather than a validated signature. These findings identify a whole-blood transcriptional signal associated with EVD-S status, supporting further investigation of transcriptomic profiling to characterize post-Ebola biological changes. Independent validation and linkage with immune functions and clinical outcomes are required before its effectiveness for routine clinical survivor monitoring can be reliably assessed.

title: The piR-016176 candidate small RNA modulates pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell phenotypes with SAP18 as a functional downstream effector.
abstract: PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) have been implicated in tumor biology, but the roles of piRNA-annotated small RNAs in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the cellular effects and molecular associations of piR-016176, a piRNA-annotated small-RNA candidate, in PDAC. Array-based profiling was performed in 10 paired PDAC and adjacent tissues, followed by qRT-PCR validation in an independent cohort of 50 paired specimens. Gain- and loss-of-function assays evaluated cellular phenotypes, while quantitative proteomics and bidirectional rescue experiments assessed the contribution of SAP18. PIWIL1 RIP-qPCR, exploratory acetylome profiling following SAP18 depletion, and integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analysis following piR-016176 overexpression were also performed. The sequence annotated as piR-016176 showed significantly lower abundance in PDAC tissues and cell lines. Mimic transfection reduced cell viability, wound closure, and Matrigel invasion while increasing apoptosis; inhibitor treatment produced opposite effects. SAP18 protein abundance changed reciprocally, and bidirectional rescue experiments supported its contribution to cell viability and Matrigel invasion. Following mimic transfection, piR-016176 and SAP18 mRNA were enriched in PIWIL1 immunoprecipitates. SAP18 depletion yielded 185 nominally altered acetylome features, none significant after multiple-testing correction, with associated proteins enriched for RNA-regulatory and mitochondrial metabolic functions. Integrating transcriptomic and proteomic data identified 112 concordantly upregulated targets enriched for interferon- and immune-related gene sets after piR-016176 overexpression. Our findings identify piR-016176 as a piRNA-annotated small-RNA candidate that modulates PDAC cell phenotypes, with SAP18 contributing to its effects on cell viability and Matrigel invasion. PIWIL1-associated RNA enrichment and exploratory acetylome and interferon-related signatures provide additional molecular clues for future investigation. Although its endogenous identity as a mature PIWI-associated piRNA remains to be established, these findings offer a foundation for further characterization of piR-016176 and its associated regulatory mechanisms in PDAC.

title: Integrated Plasma Proteomic and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Profiling of Three COVID-19 Second-Booster Regimens: An Exploratory Analysis of a Randomized Phase IV Trial.
abstract: Waning vaccine-induced immunity and the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants have prompted the evaluation of alternative booster strategies. We investigated the systemic immune profiles associated with three second-booster regimens in adults previously vaccinated with three doses of an inactivated vaccine. This exploratory analysis was nested within a randomized phase IV trial comparing homologous CoronaVac (ICV), intramuscular Ad5-nCoV (IM), and inhaled Ad5-nCoV (IH) boosting. Serum antibody responses were assessed, 119 plasma samples underwent Olink inflammatory-protein profiling, and 24 peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples were analyzed by single-cell RNA sequencing. At Day 14, wild-type SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody geometric mean titers were 880.8, 297.6, and 77.3 in the IM, IH, and ICV groups, respectively. Seven inflammatory proteins were upregulated in both Ad5-nCoV groups, and several were positively associated with antibody responses. In the small scRNA-seq subset, the IH group showed a higher observed peripheral CD8+ T cell proportion than the IM and ICV groups, together with antigen presentation- and cytotoxicity-related transcriptional patterns; neither vaccine-specific lymphocyte responses nor cellular function was directly measured. The three booster regimens were associated with distinct Day 14 humoral, inflammatory protein, and peripheral immune cell profiles. These hypothesis-generating observations complement the immunogenicity findings of the parent trial but do not establish a causal mechanism or identify a clinically preferred booster regimen.

title: Transcriptomic Discovery and Regulatory Network Prediction in Childhood Infectious Diarrhea: Cross-Cohort Assessment of Whole-Blood Pathway Concordance.
abstract: Whole-blood transcriptomics can characterize systemic responses to childhood infectious diarrhea, but exploratory regulatory predictions and candidate genes require independent assessment. We first reanalyzed pediatric whole-blood RNA sequencing data (GSE69529) using differential expression, functional enrichment, protein-association and miRNA networks, promoter sequence motifs, and inferred transcription factor activity. We subsequently compared discovery-stage pathway patterns with the independently published whole-blood microarray study GSE276395 (278 profiles). In the discovery analysis, 7050 of 15,740 analyzed genes had adjusted p < 0.05. Enrichment implicated immune signaling, RNA metabolism, cell-cycle control, intracellular organization, apoptosis, trafficking, and metabolism. The regulatory predictions did not yield motifs or transcription factors meeting corrected significance thresholds. The external publication described partly concordant innate-immune, neutrophil-centered, and immunometabolic responses, but the compared 12-gene candidate lists had no exact overlap. The cohorts differed in age, etiology, assay platform, and inclusion of noninfectious inflammatory disease. No harmonized raw data meta-analysis, leukocyte deconvolution in the present reanalysis, or experimental validation was performed. The data support a hypothesis of shared, nonspecific whole-blood inflammatory and metabolic programs; individual candidate genes and inferred regulatory mechanisms remain unvalidated.

title: Cross-cohort multi-omics evidence of elevated mitotic gene expression in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Reproducible tumor-associated expression does not establish gene-specific prognostic value. We evaluated mitotic gene expression in two discovery cohorts, three external transcriptomic cohorts and complementary proteomic resources. Pairing-aware discovery identified 384 directionally concordant genes and seven network-prioritized candidates fixed before external evaluation. All 382 measurable discovery genes showed consistent significance in the external RNA-sequencing cohort, compared with 98.3% and 93.0% of genes selected in only one discovery cohort. Paired protein measurements supported elevated TOP2A, UBE2C and CENPF, did not confirm MELK and did not measure the other three candidates. TOP2A and UBE2C protein associations with overall survival persisted after adjustment for a six-protein proliferation proxy. Neighboring mitotic genes also showed survival associations, limiting the specificity of the selected seven. For CDC20 RNA, proliferation adjustment widened the TCGA confidence interval without reducing the hazard-ratio estimate; multiplicity-adjusted significance depended on model specification and test family. The fixed seven-gene score showed clinical-adjusted overall-survival associations in both transcriptomic cohorts, retaining proliferation-adjusted evidence in TCGA. These findings are consistent with elevated mitotic gene expression in bulk LUAD tissues. They do not establish LUAD specificity, unique information for the selected seven genes, functional dependence or clinical utility.

title: Integrated bulk, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses identify Crot-associated proximal-tubule peroxisomal dysregulation in murine renal ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) underlies acute kidney injury after transplantation, shock, and major surgery. Proximal-tubule metabolic dysfunction shapes injury and repair. Peroxisomes shorten fatty acids and export products, but their cross-omic behavior in acute renal IRI remains unclear. We integrated two murine bulk RNA-sequencing discovery cohorts and two validation cohorts. Dataset-adjusted differential expression, pathway analysis, and training-only feature selection defined peroxisome-associated candidates. Nested validation assessed selection and predictive performance separately. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing resolved cellular localization, animal-level pseudobulk, and pseudotime dynamics. Segment 3 proximal-tubule (PTS3) expression informed a metabolic model for in silico Crot knockout. Spatial, proteomic, and patient-level human analyses assessed tissue distribution and cross-layer support. The discovery cohorts yielded 1,477 differentially expressed genes, with negative enrichment of peroxisome and fatty-acid programs. Crot decreased and Acot5 increased across external mouse cohorts. Nested L1 models retained Crot in 40/50 fits and Acot5 in none. Crot decreased within PTS3 at all IRI time points; its animal-aware pseudotime association was weaker and heterogeneous. Without exogenous octanoate, simulated Crot knockout reduced C8-carnitine output capacity by 18.2%-50.6%. Additional spatial cohorts supported lower whole-section Crot, with cohort-dependent proximal-tubule-rich results. Proteomics showed lower acute CROT abundance, replicated in an independent cohort with three mice per group (3 d, FDR = 0.006). Human GSE210622 showed lower proximal-tubule CROT, with sensitivity to control source; three other human contexts did not reproduce this decrease, indicating limited cross-cohort consistency. Acute murine renal IRI is accompanied by suppression of proximal-tubule peroxisomal lipid-handling programs. Convergent bulk, single-nucleus, metabolic-modeling, spatial, and protein evidence prioritizes Crot for mechanistic investigation.

title: From metabolic remodeling to therapeutic intervention: research progress on SLC7A5 in cancer.
abstract: Solute Carrier Family 7 Member 5 (SLC7A5) is a key member of the solute carrier transporter family that mediates the transmembrane transport of large neutral amino acids (LNAAs). Its expression is precisely regulated by a multilayered network encompassing transcription factors, non-coding RNAs, and RNA/protein epigenetic modifications. In various malignant tumors, SLC7A5 drives amino acid metabolic reprogramming by taking up essential amino acids (EAAs) such as leucine to activate the Mammalian Target of Rapamycin Complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling pathway. Concurrently, SLC7A5 is deeply involved in tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), ferroptosis, redox homeostasis, epigenetic modification, and integrated stress response (ISR), and is closely associated with tumor proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and poor prognosis. In solid tumors such as colorectal cancer (CRC) and breast cancer, SLC7A5 exhibits dual value as both a prognostic biomarker and a therapeutic target. Highly selective inhibitors represented by JPH203 have completed early-phase clinical trials in biliary tract cancer. However, adaptive drug resistance, systemic immunotoxicity, and individualized patient selection remain key challenges facing its clinical translation. This review systematically summarizes the regulatory mechanisms of SLC7A5, its molecular functions in driving tumor progression, the clinical significance in different solid tumors, and recent advances in targeted inhibitors development and therapeutic strategy optimization, aiming to provide a theoretical basis and clinical reference for precision metabolic intervention targeting SLC7A5.

title: Expression Changes in a Preoperative Cerebrospinal Fluid Protein Signature of Perioperative Neurocognitive Disorders and the Influence of Perioperative Administration of Fucoidan.
abstract: Postoperative neurocognitive disorder is a common complication that primarily affects senile patients and is associated with increased morbidity/mortality after surgery. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of the associated risk factors, including types of surgery and anesthesia, baseline status before surgery, and biomarkers of cognitive function, have led to ambiguous conclusions, which complicate the understanding of pathogenesis and limit the strategies for the prevention/treatment of this condition. In this study, a panel of 12 preoperative cerebrospinal fluid protein markers that displayed high predictive accuracy of postoperative delirium was revealed by a LASSO logistic regression analysis of the proteomic data from 24 matched pairs of patients. Functional enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment in immune regulation in these proteins. Further expression analysis displayed a sustained differential expression of some of these genes up to one month after surgery in the brains of mice with postoperative neurocognitive disorder, suggesting potential prognostic roles for these biomarkers. Given the well-recognized anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory functions of fucoidan, the potential influence of the perioperative administration of fucoidan on immune-related gene expression was investigated in mouse brains and PBMCs using quantitative PCR and RNA-seq, respectively. Our results showed that perioperative administration of fucoidan partially restored the gene expression pattern of the immune-related gene signatures in mouse PBMCs as well as in mouse brains.

title: ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D Are associated with urea cycle activity and ammonia stress responses in prostate cancer.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PRAD) progression is closely associated with metabolic reprogramming, but the role of nitrogen metabolism and ammonia-associated cell death remains unclear. This study investigates the clinical and functional significance of urea cycle activity in PRAD. Transcriptomic data from TCGA-PRAD and single-cell RNA-seq dataset GSE221603 were analyzed. ssGSEA was used to quantify urea cycle activity. Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, survival analysis, and multiple machine learning algorithms were applied to identify key genes. Immune infiltration, pathway enrichment, and single-cell functional analyses were performed. Experimental validation was conducted using siRNA knockdown, qPCR, Western blot, CCK-8, apoptosis assays, and NH4Cl-induced ammonia stress models. Higher urea cycle scores were associated with longer progression-free survival, although the association with progression-free survival was not significant after adjustment for StromalScore or tumor purity. Urea cycle scores were associated with distinct immune infiltration patterns and metabolic pathway reprogramming. Multi-algorithm integration identified ADRA1D and PGM5 as candidate genes associated with the urea cycle phenotype, with single-cell analyses revealing differences in their expression across cellular populations. A putative ADAMTS9-AS1/miR-183-3p/ADRA1D regulatory axis was identified and associated with urea cycle activity and cellular responses to ammonia-associated stress. ADAMTS9-AS1 knockdown reduced ADRA1D expression, decreased intracellular arginine levels, and enhanced cellular sensitivity to NH₄Cl-associated stress. Urea cycle activity is associated with a favorable metabolic phenotype in PRAD and may contribute to cellular adaptation to ammonia stress. ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D may represent candidate genes associated with this metabolic network, providing potential targets for further investigation of nitrogen metabolism in prostate cancer.

title: Associations Between Coal Dust Exposure and Coal Workers' Pneumoconiosis Among Coal Workers: Insights from Mediation Analysis of S100A8.
abstract: Long-term coal dust exposure in confined environments leads to lung function decline and increases the risk of Coal Workers' Pneumoconiosis (CWP) among miners. This study assessed associations between multi-omics-identified metabolites and CWP incidence. Firstly, Single-Cell RNA-Seq screening (scRNA-seq) was performed to screen differentially expressed genes in fibrotic lung tissues from CWP mouse models. After identifying 41 human homologous genes, antibody array and ELISA were used to screen out six candidate protein biomarkers (IL-6, MIP-1β, CXCL2, CYR61, CFH and S100A8), and then a retrospective case-control study nested within an occupational cohort was performed, which included 397 male miners. Generalized linear models and exploratory mediation analysis were used to analyze data. Our results showed a clear dose-response relationship. Exploratory mediation analysis revealed specific biomarker effects. S100 calcium-binding protein A8 (S100A8) mediated 27.0% to 40.4% of the association of the exposure-lung function decline, and 23.7% of the association of the exposure and the risk of CWP. This study identified S100A8 as the potential statistical mediator in the association between coal dust exposure and lung function decline/CWP. Moreover, these two serum proteins can potentially serve as clinical biomarkers for CWP.

title: Transcriptomic Profiling of Convergent and Divergent Macrophage Polarization in Myocardial Infarction and Takotsubo Syndrome.
abstract: To compare, at the transcriptomic level, the infiltration characteristics and transcriptional differences of cardiac macrophages at 24 h after modeling between myocardial infarction (MI) and Takotsubo syndrome (TTS). Bulk RNA-seq data obtained 1 h and 24 h after modeling, and single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data obtained 24 h after modeling, from mouse models of MI and TTS were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differential expression analysis and pathway enrichment analysis were performed on the bulk RNA-seq data, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed to identify hub genes. scRNA-seq data were used for macrophage re-clustering, integrative comparison and hdWGCNA analysis. Protein expression was assessed by Western blotting and immunofluorescence in MI and TTS rat models. Bulk RNA sequencing revealed that MI was characterized predominantly by neutrophil chemotaxis and inflammatory cascades in the early phase, whereas TTS displayed type I interferon responses and antiviral-like immune transcriptional features. PPI network analysis identified that the hub genes in MI were enriched for AP-1 transcription factors and pro-inflammatory cytokines, while those in TTS were almost exclusively interferon-stimulated genes. Single-cell sequencing showed that both neutrophils and macrophages infiltrated the myocardium in MI and TTS, with neutrophils predominating in MI and macrophages in TTS; integrated analysis further showed that MI associated macrophages exhibited pro-fibrotic transcriptional features, whereas TTS associated macrophages displayed pro-inflammatory and oxidative stress transcriptional features. hdWGCNA identified tissue remodeling modules in MI and pro-inflammatory modules in TTS, and highlighted upregulation of Ifih1 and Ccrl2 in TTS and of S100a9 in MI. At 24 h after modeling, MI associated macrophages displayed pro-fibrotic transcriptional features, whereas TTS associated macrophages displayed stress and inflammation related transcriptional features. These transcriptional differences may be related to the divergent ventricular remodeling that follows in each disease. Ccrl2 and Ifih1 in TTS and S100a9 in MI are candidate genes warranting further functional validation.

title: Integrative blood transcriptomic analysis identifies IFIT3 as a candidate biomarker associated with host immune responses in tuberculosis.
abstract: Blood-based host-response biomarkers may complement pathogen-directed tests for tuberculosis (TB). We integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses with clinical validation to identify immune-related blood biomarkers, focusing on interferon-induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats 3 (IFIT3). Four peripheral-blood microarray datasets (GSE42834, GSE83456, GSE19491, and GSE19439) were analyzed using GEO2R. Differentially expressed genes were evaluated by protein-protein interaction analysis, functional enrichment, immune-cell deconvolution, and gene set enrichment analysis. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were used to characterize candidate-gene expression across immune-cell populations. IFIT3 expression was assessed by RT-qPCR in a small independent cohort of 10 patients with TB and 11 healthy controls. The analysis identified 96 shared differentially expressed genes and eight key interferon-related genes: STAT1, IFIT3, IFI44, OAS2, IFIT2, RSAD2, XAF1, and OAS1. TB samples showed lower estimated proportions of CD8+ T cells and resting CD4+ memory T cells and higher proportions of monocytes, activated dendritic cells, and neutrophils. Across the available human PBMC single-cell data, IFIT3 was detected across several innate and adaptive immune-cell populations. In the small independent cohort, RT-qPCR showed higher IFIT3 expression in TB samples, with a preliminary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.763. IFIT3 is a candidate blood-based host-response biomarker associated with TB-related immune responses, while its clinical utility remains to be established in larger prospective cohorts and clinically relevant control groups.

title: Comprehensive single-cell and spatial transcriptome landscapes of ferroptosis regulators in ccRCC reveal intercellular interactions within malignant cells and DERL3 + plasma cells via JAK2/STAT3/GPX4 axis.
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) ranks among the most common malignant tumors affecting the urinary tract. However, the role of ferroptosis mediated by plasma cells in ccRCC remains poorly understood. In this study, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomic RNA sequencing (spRNA-seq), bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis to investigate the comprehensive landscapes of ferroptosis regulators within ccRCC. Expression profiles of ferroptosis markers, drivers and suppressors were depicted in scRNA-seq data via Addmodule Score and Percentage Feature Set algorithms. The marker genes and RNA-seq data were utilized to construct the Plasma Signature (Plasma.Sig), predicting overall survival (OS) of ccRCC patients with machine learning (ML) algorithms. In vitro and in vivo experiments were conducted to validate our bioinformatics findings. Through scRNA-seq and spRNA-seq analyses, we identified a subpopulation of DERL3 + plasma cells with close intercellular interactions with malignant cells, which is also correlated with ferroptosis suppressors in ccRCC. Utilizing marker genes of DERL3 + plasma cells, we developed the Plasma.Sig to predict OS of ccRCC patients accurately and specifically. By bulk RNA-seq analysis, we demonstrated that high DERL3 expression was associated with poor prognosis in ccRCC. Co-culture experiments revealed that knockdown of DERL3 in plasma cells decreased GPX4 expression in ccRCC tumor cells at both mRNA and protein levels. Furthermore, DERL3 knockdown impaired tumor cell proliferation, enhanced lipid peroxidation, and significantly induced ferroptosis in ccRCC tumor cells through the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway. Notably, combining DERL3 targeting with anti-PD-1 therapy enhanced the efficacy of immunotherapy in subcutaneous tumor model of ccRCC. Using multi-omics approaches, we identify that targeting DERL3 in plasma cells modulates tumor ferroptosis via the JAK2/STAT3 axis and potentiates immunotherapy response in ccRCC. Our findings highlight ferroptosis-targeting strategies combined with immunotherapy as a promising therapeutic approach for ccRCC. Not applicable.
